extracted.intended_audience: writers and poets (students of literature and authors seeking classical maxims on style)
extracted.subtask_description: A compact collection of classical maxims and aphorisms about composition, diction, character, and the aims of poetry and prose — suitable as prescriptive guidance for writing verse and literary prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity / consistent plan
rubrics_metrics.description: "Keep one consistent plan from end to end." (Hor. Ars Poet. v. 126)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates structural unity: maintain a single coherent plan or design throughout a poem or piece to preserve focus and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity / concision
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let brevity dispatch the rapid thought." (Hor. 1 Sat. x. 9)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise expression; dispatch ideas swiftly rather than over-elaborating. Encourages trimming excess to keep tone and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude / believable fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fictions, to please, should wear the face of truth." (Hor. Ars Poet. v. 338)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even invented material should appear true and plausible to the reader; realism or convincing detail increases pleasure and persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than tell / visual impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "What we hear moves less than what we see." (Hor. Ars Poet. 180)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize vivid sensory (especially visual) detail over mere narration; sensory description has stronger emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional effect / captivate the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Tis not enough a poem's finely writ; It must affect and captivate the soul." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 99)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical elegance alone is insufficient — a work must move readers emotionally and engage them at depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness / follow nature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Keep Nature's great original in view, And thence the living images pursue." (Hor. Ars Poet. 327)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base imagery, character, and behaviour on observation of nature and human life; avoid artificiality and affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe manners / character authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Note well the manners." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 156)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately render social manners, customs, and character traits — fidelity to human behaviour makes fiction credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of elevated elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Never presume to make a god appear, But for a business worthy of a god." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 191)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use highly elevated, mythical, or supernatural devices only when the subject truly warrants them; avoid gratuitous grandeur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid grandiose diction / inflated words
rubrics_metrics.description: "Forgets his swelling and gigantic words." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 97)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject unnecessarily pompous or bombastic vocabulary; prefer language that suits the subject and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit language and style to character
rubrics_metrics.description: "He knows what best befits each character." (Hor. Ars Poet. v. 316)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure register, diction, and speech patterns match characters' social station, temperament, and situation; consistency aids verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invent words cautiously / limited licence
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you would unheard-of things express, Invent new words; we can indulge a muse, Until the licence rise to an abuse." (Hor. Ars Poet. v. 48)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coinage and neologism are permissible but should be used sparingly and only when they serve expressive need, else they become distracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend instruction with delight (didactic balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "But he who blends instruction with delight, Wins every reader, nor in vain shall write." (Hor. Ars Poet. v. 341)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When teaching or moralizing, combine useful insight with entertainment and stylistic charm so the work engages rather than lectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for minor errors in otherwise elegant work
rubrics_metrics.description: "But in a poem elegantly writ, I will not quarrel with a slight mistake, Such as our nature's frailty may excuse." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 351)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work that succeeds stylistically and emotionally can excuse small imperfections; evaluate faults in context of overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection / avoid vulgar default
rubrics_metrics.description: "To write on vulgar themes, is thought an easy task." (Hor. 2 Ep. i. 168)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing coarse or trivial themes may be easier but is often viewed as less ambitious; select subject matter deliberately if aiming for higher art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer lively, living images over empty loftiness
rubrics_metrics.description: "But (to avoid such meanness) soaring high, With empty sound, and airy notions fly." (Hor. Ars Poet. ver. 227, adapted)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vacuous grandiosity — elevated style should be grounded in sense and imagery rather than empty rhetorical swell.
